claims.text_en: Kamphaeng Phet is an underground MRT Blue Line station, code BL12, opened 3 July 2004 beneath Kamphaeng Phet Road in Chatuchak district (13.797693 N, 100.548361 E per the article; OSM node 13.79795, 100.54788), between Chatuchak Park (BL13) and Bang Sue, with 1,164,679 passengers in 2021 — the lowest of the three Chatuchak-area rail stops. An underground mall (MetroMall) opened at the station in early 2009. The road is named for Prince of Kamphaeng Phet, the first Thai commander of the State Railway; the station shares its name with a province, and with an SRT Dark Red Line station (RN02) about 3 km north on Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road.

geography.notes: App anchor 13.8049 sits ~770 m north of the OSM node, close to Chatuchak Park MRT — reconcile anchor convention.

evidence.paraphrase: BL12, opened 3 Jul 2004, beneath Kamphaeng Phet Rd, Chatuchak district, coords, neighbours Chatuchak Park and Bang Sue, 1,164,679 passengers 2021, MetroMall opened early 2009, road named for the prince.
OSM tags Kamphaeng Phet ref=BL12 at 13.79795/100.54788, operator BEM.
The separate SRT Dark Red 'Chatuchak' station (RN02) is on Kamphaeng Phet 2 Rd at Nikhom KM.11, coords 13.8265/100.5494.

limitations: Underlying article is an unsourced stub; ridership not corroborated by a second read source.

claims.text_en: The operator's own station page defines the unit's front doors: Exit 1 — Chatuchak Weekend Market and the Mo Chit transport connection; Exit 2 — the market, Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road, Bang Sue Junction; Exit 3 — Or Tor Kor (A.T.K.) market, Kamphaeng Phet 1 Road, the Dairy Promotion Organisation, Wat Phai Tan. Buses stop at exits 1 and 3 (routes 49, 96, 134, 136, 138, 145, 509, 536 on the DD Mall side; 77, 96, 134, 136, 145, 509, 517, A1 across from it), with motorcycle-taxi stands at all three exits and a lift at Exit 2.

temporal_scope.notes: Bus route lists change; operator page is the authority.

claims.text_en: Transport 10 — the plausible mechanism is market-and-bus adjacency rather than rail redundancy: this is an MRT-only stop with no BTS interchange of its own (the BTS transfer is one stop away at Chatuchak Park BL13), yet it has direct underground-market access, two bus clusters with roughly a dozen routes including the A1 corridor service, and the Or Tor Kor daily market at Exit 3. Nothing read measures station-level connectivity quality; the 10 should be read as the app's rubric applied to this asset set, and the coordinator should confirm the rubric's basis.

geography.notes: MRT-only status is the tension: no read source calls this the area's best-connected point; the market/bus asset set is what distinguishes it.

claims.text_en: The unit's rhythm is the weekend market's: the blocks around Exits 1-2 host the Chatuchak Weekend Market — about 35 acres, 26-27 sections, with 200,000+ weekend visitors by the market site's count — while Or Tor Kor at Exit 3 trades daily with a morning peak and thins through the afternoon. Weekday Kamphaeng Phet is therefore a market-employee and produce-logistics day, in sharp contrast to the Saturday-Sunday visitor surge; no read source quantifies weekday footfall.

claims.text_en: Or Tor Kor (A.T.K.) market, at Exit 3, is run by the Marketing Organisation for Farmers and is described in the neighbourhood guide as 'the fresh market Bangkok recommends to itself' — graded and curated produce, seafood on ice, a large prepared-food section, covered and partly air-conditioned, expensive by Bangkok fresh-market standards. A widely repeated claim ranks it 4th-best fresh market in the world (CNN, 2017), but the CNN page now returns 404 and the rank could not be body-verified here — treat it as unverified heritage.

claims.text_en: The long-distance bus edge of this unit's story is real but bounded: BEM lists the Mo Chit transport connection at Exit 1, while the actual Mo Chit 2 terminal (Bangkok Bus Terminal, Chatuchak — northern, Central and Isan routes, opened 8 April 1998) sits at 999 Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road behind Queen Sirikit Park, roughly 2 km from the Chatuchak-area rail stations per the terminal's article — outside this 800 m catchment. In 2025 the Transport Ministry was reported weighing consolidation of all three long-distance terminals at Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal.

geography.notes: Do not credit the terminal to this unit's walkshed; the Exit-1 label is a connection point, not the terminal.

temporal_scope.notes: Relocation talk has recurred for years without execution.

preview.text_en: A specialist stop with the market's doors built into it: BL12's exits open onto Chatuchak Weekend Market (200,000+ weekend visitors) and the daily Or Tor Kor premium market, with a dozen bus routes at two stops — while the famous park block that lifts its green score actually sits in the neighbouring units, 1.1-1.5 km out by centroid.

guide_lead.text_en: Kamphaeng Phet (MRT BL12, opened 2004) is the market's own station: Exit 1-2 drop into Chatuchak Weekend Market's 35 acres, Exit 3 into Or Kor Tor's graded, air-conditioned produce halls, and bus bays with roughly a dozen routes sit at the exits — a transport-10 built on adjacency and buses rather than rail variety, since the BTS interchange is one stop north at Chatuchak Park. Rents track the Chatuchak blend (16,000-25,000 baht studios and small one-beds captured district-wide). The honest caveats: the 0.1 ha of mapped park means green 9 is buffer effect from parks centred in other units, the unit's nightlife and safety scores have no found evidence either way, and the market itself is mid-redevelopment after City Hall's 2025 clock-tower evictions.

strengths.text_en: Unmatched market access for a rail stop: direct exits into the weekend market and the daily Or Tor Kor market, plus roughly a dozen bus routes at two on-street stops.
MetroMall underground and a compact station footprint keep errands indoor-adjacent in rain or heat, at the district's mid-market rent level.

tradeoffs.text_en: MRT-only: no BTS interchange at the station (one stop away at BL13), ridership one-sixth of the neighbouring interchange, and the transport 10 depends on market/bus adjacency — confirm the rubric.
Green 9 is borrowed scenery: 0.1 ha mapped in-unit and no park centroid within 850 m; the park complex's centroids lie 1.1-1.5 km away in the mo-chit/chatuchak units.

day_night.text_en: Weekdays belong to market logistics and Or Kor Tor's morning trade; Saturdays-Sundays the unit absorbs a 200,000-visitor surge that starts at the station exits and drains outward.

within_area_variation.text_en: The unit splits between the market's south-western edge (exits 1-2, weekend economy) and the Kamphaeng Phet 1 Road strip (exit 3, daily market, temple and school), with the park complex beyond the boundary to the west.

conditional_fit.text_en: Fit for market traders and staff, produce buyers, and bus-to-MRT transfer riders who value the market on the doorstep.
Poor fit for those who want the park as a daily amenity inside their own unit, multi-line rail variety, or verified nightlife.
